content_of_post_to_comment:
I already don’t like social media, I only have Facebook and YouTube. Reddit as well, but I mostly use it to ask questions and get answers about different things. Facebook I only use for the people in my life that use it. My biggest vice is YouTube, I’m a big gamer and I watch a lot of gaming videos.

I don’t necessarily want to give that up, but I do see the value in limiting and being more conscious of my screen time.

Technology will always be part of my life. I’m in college for computer science and I do like tech for the most part. But I hate the mindless scrolling that some people do, myself included though I’m not that bad, and I find myself getting annoyed at stupid comments way too often. I recognize that internet comments aren’t worth my time and energy, but I’m not able to shut that off unless I just don’t look at them.

What would some of you recommend when it comes to being online the bare minimum and not getting distracted by scrolling when I do? I am typing this on an iPhone and I plan to get an android eventually so I can strictly control what I use it for. But how should I approach this in the meantime?

There are plenty of things I want to do with my time, both personally and relating to my future field(like personal coding projects etc). Being on the internet and watching videos/shorts/reels, along with my other responsibilities, makes it hard to dedicate time and brain power to making those things happen. I just want to be a lot more intentional with my time. I’m pretty young so I’m not super worried about it, but the sooner I start the better off I’ll be at time management.

Just a big rant and questions. It’s a confusing thing because I will always be involved with tech, but I want to avoid mindless consumerism as much as possible.

Appreciate any responses!
comment: The YouTube/gaming part is probably the hardest one to solve because it’s not just a “bad habit” when it’s also something you genuinely enjoy. I found it helps to separate intentional use from default use: decide what you want to watch or play before opening the app, rather than letting the algorithm pick. Also, don’t underestimate replacing scrolling with tiny coding sessions; 20 focused minutes can build momentum.
